items.title: Dave Liebman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I got into Panallal Ghosh, all those guys, [?] Khan.

ctx.x: . . . Within You, Without You. But here’s the thing – and Ashirbad is on there. That’s wisdom – Indian music, in the end, is the heaviest shit, period, done. I was – now, everything is so clichéd, because of World Music, but then it was exciting. I wasn’t the first to do it. Oregon and like that. And look, Eric Dolphy did a record with a tablā player in 1961. It’s just that I really got into it. I studied bansuri. I got the flute. I got into Panallal Ghosh, all those guys, [?] Khan. I got into it. And Badal said,…

Badal became my man. He was my main guy. He’s still very close with me. Badal was older. Badal was different from the other guys. He came from a different culture. He was – he started out as an accountant. He never played tablās until he came here. Went down on 6th Street and Second Avenue, Indian restaurants. “Oh, you play tablās?” “Sure, I play tablās. I play tablās.” That’s how John met him. That’s how McLaughlin met him, going there to eat. Badal became very – he helped me be a leader of the band. I don’t…
